columns.rationale: tailnum has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 3322, exactly matching the table's row_count of 3322, making it a reliable unique aircraft identifier.
year is landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample (1956.0-2013.0) is an integral value, so it casts cleanly to INTEGER; null_rate is 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows null) so it stays nullable.
type has null_rate 0.0 and only 3 distinct_values (Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft), so it is kept as a required categorical string.
manufacturer has null_rate 0.0 and 35 distinct values including AIRBUS and BOEING from the samples, so it is kept as required.
model has null_rate 0.0 and 127 distinct values (samples include 150, 172E, 310Q), so it is kept as required.
engines is DECIMAL(38,9) but distinct_values are exactly [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], all integral, with null_rate 0.0, so it casts to INTEGER and stays required.
seats ranges from min 2.0 to max 450.0 with all sampled values integral (2.0-12.0 shown) and null_rate 0.0, so it casts to INTEGER and stays required.

speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null) but the 13 distinct_values present (90.0-432.0) are all integral, so it casts to INTEGER while remaining nullable; the column is sparsely populated.
engine has null_rate 0.0 with 6 distinct_values (4 Cycle, Reciprocating, Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet, Turbo-prop, Turbo-shaft), so it is kept as required.
_airbyte_raw_id is marked is_airbyte_metadata true and is a capture-tool artifact, so it is dropped.
_airbyte_extracted_at is marked is_airbyte_metadata true with a single constant value (2026-09-02T23:26:22), so it is dropped as a capture-tool artifact.
_airbyte_meta is marked is_airbyte_metadata true with the single constant value {}, so it is dropped as a capture-tool artifact.

decisions.rationale: tailnum has distinct_count 3322 exactly equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so it uniquely identifies each aircraft row and is declared the grain.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is applied.
All sampled year values (1956.0-2013.0) are integral, justifying a cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.
engines distinct_values are exactly [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], all integral, justifying a cast to INTEGER.
seats samples (2.0-12.0) and the min/max range (2.0-450.0) are all integral, justifying a cast to INTEGER.
speed distinct_values (90.0-432.0) are all integral but null_rate is 0.993076, so the column casts to INTEGER while remaining nullable and sparsely populated.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are each marked is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows), a modest but nonzero rate, so nulls are retained rather than imputed or failed.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows null), so the column is retained as sparsely populated rather than dropped or imputed.

purpose: This table provides a cleaned, deduplicated reference of aircraft tail numbers and their airframe/engine characteristics (manufacturer, model, year, engine configuration, seats) to support joins against flight event tables in downstream analytics.
usage: Join on tailnum to enrich flight records with aircraft attributes; treat year and speed as nullable and filter or coalesce them explicitly before aggregation, and be aware speed is populated for less than 1% of rows so it is unsuitable as a primary analytic field without further sourcing.
limitations: speed is null for 99.3076% of rows (3299 of 3322) and should not be relied on for broad analysis; year is missing for 2.1072% of rows; no duplicate rows were found in bronze (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was needed, but this was not independently re-verified beyond the profile's reported rate.
